💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United are set to welcome Luke Shaw and Karl Darlow back into the fold for tomorrow night’s Champions League trip to Sporting, but they will be without Matheus Cunha, who was left out of the travelling cohort.
  • The Brazilian was withdrawn at half time in the 4-0 drubbing from Liverpool over the weekend, replaced by Joshua Zirkzee as the Red Devils trailed 2-0 and were down to ten men after Leny Yoro’s now-overturned red card.
  • The former Wolves forward is sidelined due to a suspension he picked up from his red card against Roma last time out in Europe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United are set to welcome Luke Shaw and Karl Darlow back into the fold for tomorrow night’s Champions League trip to Sporting, but they will be without Matheus Cunha, who was left out of the travelling cohort.

The Brazilian was withdrawn at half time in the 4-0 drubbing from Liverpool over the weekend, replaced by Joshua Zirkzee as the Red Devils trailed 2-0 and were down to ten men after Leny Yoro’s now-overturned red card.

The former Wolves forward is sidelined due to a suspension he picked up from his red card against Roma last time out in Europe.

The return of Shaw, meanwhile, will be appreciated by new boss Mauricio Pochettino, who has the enviable task of shaping a defence that has conceded 34 goals in 18 matches so far this season.

The left-back has missed United’s last eight fixtures with a muscular matter, but the former Southampton defender was pictured in training ahead of Wednesday night’s game.

The 31-year-old is yet to feature in the Champions League this season, rested for the 4-0 win in the opener over Sabah, before injury ruled him out of the next three fixtures.

Backup goalkeeper Darlow has made just one appearance for the Red Devils since joining from rivals Leeds in the summer.

The Welshman was called up for international duty a fortnight ago, playing the first game of the break against Norway before being rested for the second due to a knock.

Darlow was not fit enough to be named on the bench for Sunday’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield, but the 36-year-old was also spotted in training ahead of the Sporting game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Steven Gerrard admits he is struggling to understand Xabi Alonso’s refusal to utilise one of Chelsea’s key summer signings.

After some encouraging early signs, the Blues have fallen off the title pace being set by Arsenal and have suffered several damaging defeats in recent weeks.

A rare home loss against Tottenham was compounded by Saturday’s drubbing at the hands of Leeds United at Stamford Bridge when defensive shortcomings were to the fore once again.

Alonso has refused to use injuries as an excuse for an alarming dip in form but the absences of Reece James and Joao Pedro are being keenly felt.

The Brazil international striker is particularly key component of Chelsea’s system, but cover was sourced during the summer window in the shape of the experienced Danny Welbeck.

Alonso, however, has appeared strangely reluctant to start the 35-year-old in Pedro’s absence, with Pedro Neto preferred on occasion while against Leeds he chose to hand a starting opportunity to the largely untried Emmanuel Emegha.

‘Especially with Joao Pedro out, you’re thinking it’s perfect for Danny Welbeck, and he’s an experienced player out there,’ Gerrard told The Overlap with Sky Bet when asked about his former England teammate.

‘He’s someone who can help a lot of youngsters that are playing, a lot of inexperienced players at Chelsea.

‘Same reason why they brought in Jordan Henderson, and you would say that Jordan’s done a really good job, what Xabi Alonso’s wanted him to do, but with no Joao Pedro, to not see hardly anything of Welbeck is a big surprise.

‘Unless there’s something going on that we don’t know about, whether there’s a niggle in the background or there’s a fitness glitch, I don’t know.

‘But from the Welbeck we watched at Brighton & Hove Albion, what was it, three, four months ago, the back end of last season, you would think he would be the perfect replacement for Joao Pedro being missing for such a period of time.’.

Latest Update: Chelsea stance on Xabi Alonso sack now revealed amid poor form and dressing-room 'mutiny' claims

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (431 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 24 Nov 2026 07:38.
  • Chelsea have decided against making an immediate change in the dugout despite growing pressure on manager Xabi Alonso.
  • The Blues have won just one of their last five matches, with a 4-1 defeat to Leeds United at Stamford Bridge only intensifying scrutiny of the Spaniard.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 24 Nov 2026 07:38.

Chelsea have decided against making an immediate change in the dugout despite growing pressure on manager Xabi Alonso.

The Blues have won just one of their last five matches, with a 4-1 defeat to Leeds United at Stamford Bridge only intensifying scrutiny of the Spaniard.

However, the club hierarchy are understood to remain keen to give their summer appointment time, although the next few fixtures could prove crucial.

Chelsea's board have no immediate plans to sack Alonso, but the 44-year-old is under pressure to deliver results in the coming matches, according to latest reports.

According to recent reports, the Blues face Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace next, before a demanding run of fixtures against Liverpool, Manchester City and Aston Villa. The three matches before Christmas could "make or break" Alonso's future at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea currently sit eighth in the Premier League table, with supporters having already voiced their frustration during the defeat to Leeds.

There are also concerns of a "mutiny" behind the scenes, with it believed that several players are unhappy with Alonso's coaching methods at the training ground and that there is a "terrible atmosphere in the dressing room".

According to recent reports, nevertheless, the hierarchy are understood to believe that injuries have contributed to the team's struggles. Joao Pedro has been absent since the middle of October with a thigh problem, having been an vital figure earlier in the campaign.

The club are hopeful that his return could help spark an improvement in results, although the pressure on Alonso is unlikely to disappear unless performances improve.

Clearlake have made managerial changes a regular feature of their Chelsea project, but dismissing Alonso just months into his tenure would risk repeating a familiar cycle at Stamford Bridge.

Sources indicate that the Spaniard is still relatively early into his reign and has had to contend with key absences, particularly Pedro and captain Reece James. Both are usual starters who could make a significant difference to the side, especially in a system that relies on their respective qualities.

The reported dressing-room discontent is concerning, however, and Alonso will need to address that promptly, but it should not automatically mean his position is untenable.

Managers need time to implement their ideas, build relationships and establish consistency. Chelsea have invested in Alonso and should allow him to demonstrate what he can achieve with a fitter squad.

The upcoming fixtures will undoubtedly test that patience, but another change of manager so early in the process would hardly represent a convincing long-term strategy.

Industry observers note that then the sighting of Raya the following day in Oxford Circus with his arm in a sling. And the report that he had been able to drive himself home after the club returned to London from Newcastle.

It has been revealed that the sense of panic was understandable. Raya is Arsenal’s most irreplaceable player, pivotal to the team not just because of his shot-stopping, but the way he commands his area and how central he is to the build-up in possession as well.

In a recent development, it was good news, then, that he has avoided a serious injury. Raya has not yet been ruled out of facing Manchester City this weekend.

Even with the outlook more positive than it might have been, Arsenal must still find a way to cope without the Spaniard for at least tonight’s match against Borussia Dortmund.

Recent findings suggest that this will be a big night for Kepa Arrizabalaga. He started against Kairat Almaty last season, but that dead rubber aside has not played in the Champions League since making four appearances for Real Madrid in the competition in 2023.

Recent findings suggest that this is a chance to prove he still belongs at this level. Kepa will surely still have an eye on becoming a first-choice goalkeeper again at a top club elsewhere in the seasons ahead. However, that kind of evidence has been in short supply since he arrived at Arsenal.

Industry observers note that mikel Arteta put his faith in Kepa last season in the Carabao Cup final and it was not repaid. Kepa was booked for hauling down Jeremy Doku after misjudging a bouncing ball, before gifting City the lead when spilling a cross.

Sources indicate that his distribution, too, was poor. Throughout the match, Arsenal’s build-up was almost entirely nullified by City and that started with the goalkeeper.

A key facet of Arsenal’s build-up is Raya’s ability to not just go short, but to ping flat, long passes up the pitch to play over the press when required.

It is easy to forget just how highly rated Kepa once was, he remains the most expensive goalkeeper signing of all time.

“David Raya can play six, I swear,” Noni Madueke stated in a recent interview.

Kepa cannot play those same passes with the same trajectory or accuracy. Nor is he as convincing in inspiring the same confidence when going short under pressure.

Asked on Monday whether Arsenal would have to change how they play without Raya, Arteta said: “We adapt to players’ qualities, and they all have different ones.

“There are certain things that, in our game or in the way that we understand the game and we want to play the game, everybody has to be 100% committed to, but then we make adjustments in relation to the qualities of the players.”.

One of those adjustments will have to be how Arsenal build up. Illan Meslier would be more comfortable in that respect, with the ball at his feet, but he is liable to make big mistakes and can be exposed when the ball is crossed on top of him.

There has never been any real consideration from Arteta or his coaching staff that it would be Meslier getting the nod over Kepa to stand in for Raya.

When he signed in the summer, Meslier was aware of the pecking order. He arrived primarily to allow Tommy Setford to go out on loan, rather than to replace Kepa as No2.

Meslier started in the Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood, even with Kepa fit and in the squad. However, that was due to a desire to reward Meslier for his consistency in training and impact on the squad, not a rejigging of the pecking order.

According to recent reports, it is easy to forget just how highly rated Kepa once was. He remains the most expensive goalkeeper signing of all time, joining Chelsea for £72million in 2018.

That price tag has followed him around ever since. So too Carabao Cup finals, both last season’s horror show and the 2019 edition when he refused to be substituted.

The temptation is to say a quiet night, one in which he is not noticed against Dortmund, would be ideal for Kepa, but Raya does not have many of those.

Even when he is not required to pull off saves, he is still making line-breaking passes or pushing up close to the halfway line to snuff out attacks.

Kepa failed on all those counts in the Carabao Cup final last season. Another poor performance this time and it is hard to see how he can retain Arteta’s trust.

In his biggest test since that Wembley occasion, Arsenal need Kepa to minimise the disruption of Raya’s absence.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans should not expect much transfer business to be done this winter, with Mauricio Pochettino expected to be given a meagre budget to work with in January.

The Argentine has arrived as the newly introduced Red Devils boss and took charge of his first game on Sunday, which did not go well at all as Liverpool romped to a 4-0 win over their old rivals at Anfield.

Leny Yoro was shown an early red card, leaving Pochettino’s intends in tatters as defeat left Manchester United 19th in the Premier League table.

With just one win and 23 goals conceded in 11 league outings, there have been calls for signings to be made, especially in defence.

Before Pochettino was appointed, club legend Gary Neville even urged him to turn down the job unless the hierarchy promised to sign two defenders over the winter transfer window.

That may still happen, but it will have to be some canny business as the Daily Mail reports that Manchester United will have ‘well under £50 million’ to spend in the next transfer window.

Having focused on midfield signings over the summer, United want a centre-back, left-back and striker, but obviously that cannot be done to any level of quality on such a meagre budget.

Brentford centre-back Nathan Collins has been touted as a target, but the 25-year-old would not be a cheap option.

The Bees paid £23m for him when they signed him from Wolves three years ago and he remains under contract until 2029.

The Republic of Ireland international has been a mainstay in the team since moving to Brentford, although is presently out with injury.

Summer targets at left-back included Manchester City’s Rayan Ait-Nouri and Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde, both of whom could be options again.

Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been linked with a move to Old Trafford, having worked with Pochettino in his stint as USA manager.

The former Arsenal man came close to joining Everton in a £40m deal over the summer before the deal collapsing at the last minute.

Manchester United may look to make a loan signing to keep costs down, although could stretch the budget if they feel that relegation is a genuine threat.

Recent findings suggest that neville does not think it will come to a relegation scrap, despite United’s woeful form, saying after the defeat to Liverpool: ‘I don’t believe they’re in a relegation fight. They’re second-bottom in the league, it’s as bad as it’s been for 55 years. I do think they’ll come out of it and move up the table.

However, he added: ‘You could arrogantly look at Coventry at home, or Sunderland at home, and think United will be alright. But the performance levels we’re seeing at the moment don’t give you much confidence.’.

Arsenal: 'Much more complete' - how Madueke has grown and become a key man amid injuries

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1292 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 07:45.
  • Noni Madueke's signing by Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had even stepped onto the pitch.
  • Arriving from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing and had to justify an investment in a player who initially seemed destined to be a back-up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 07:45.

Noni Madueke's signing by Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had even stepped onto the pitch.

Arriving from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing and had to justify an investment in a player who initially seemed destined to be a back-up.

A little over a year later, the debate is taking on another dimension. With Saka injured, Madueke has been given a longer run of opportunities and has taken the chance. As well as goals and assists, he has contributed in different roles on both sides of the pitch. The 2-2 draw with Newcastle, in which he scored the goal that earned Arsenal a point, was another example of this development.

Mikel Arteta has noticed a change that goes beyond productivity. In a press conference, the manager highlighted the variety that the forward has added to the team's play and his contribution without the ball. And Madueke's growth has followed a concrete path.

Madueke has very specific characteristics. Left-footed and explosive, he likes to receive the ball wide on the right, run at the full-back and carry the ball towards the box to shoot or find a team-mate. His short burst of acceleration and ability to change direction make his movements hard to defend when he receives the ball in equal-numbers situations.

Recent findings suggest that that characteristic was already visible at Chelsea. In the 2024-25 season, he was one of the Premier League players who carried the ball into the box the most and created danger mainly through individual runs. The problem was inconsistency in execution: he did not always choose the best moment. Arteta acknowledged the change.

'He is becoming decisive in games, and that is what we need from our forward players. And he is doing it in several ways, which is something I really like. He has added variety and a lot more connection to his game' - Arteta said.

The numbers help to gauge the growth. According to FotMob's analysis for the 2026-27 Premier League, Madueke creates 3.6 chances per 90 minutes, compared with 1.5 for Saka. It is a significant difference, although it is key to consider that Saka has played fewer minutes.

The improvement also indicates in his ability to contribute without the ball. According to Arteta, Madueke does not always need to receive the ball at his feet to take part in the move.

It has been revealed that 'And yes, I also love his intensity without the ball. So, I would say he is becoming a much more complete player, and I think he is enjoying it a lot' - Arteta remarked.

It has been revealed that the evolution, therefore, is not about abandoning the dribble but about knowing when to use it. Madueke remains a player of individual initiative, only now he seems to understand better how his actions can connect with the collective workings of the team.

In a recent development, the comparison with Saka is inevitable, but the two are not identical players. Both are left-footed and prefer to start from the right to cut inside, but they do so in different ways.

Saka is more refined in decision-making. He has excellent ball control, protects possession under pressure and alternates between carries, short passes and crosses very naturally. His ability to draw two markers and find the free team-mate is also one of Arsenal's main attacking tools.

Industry observers note that madueke, for his part, offers more explosiveness in the first movement and tends to look for the individual duel more often. He is a more vertical player, who likes to accelerate and attack the space left by the full-back. When he is confident, he can disorganise a defence without depending on a long build-up.

It has been revealed that the creation data helps illustrate this difference. As well as outperforming Saka in chances created per 90 minutes in FotMob's analysis, Madueke also shows a greater volume of dribbles and progressive carries per minute in another statistical comparison this season. Saka, on the other hand, keeps the advantage in shooting and defensive contribution indicators. They are complementary profiles, not necessarily competitors for a single way of playing.

Recent findings suggest that this difference is valuable for Arteta. Against opponents who defend in a low block, Saka can be more useful to control possession, combine with the midfielders and find the pass that dismantles the marking. Madueke can offer a more direct threat, attacking the full-back and creating situations of individual imbalance.

It has been revealed that the Englishman has also shown that he can play on the left, a role he performed when Christos Tzolis was unavailable. There, he needs to adapt his movements: instead of cutting inside with his dominant foot, he can look for the byline and cross with his right. It is not necessarily his ideal position, but the versatility widens Arteta's options and prevents the team from depending on a single alternative for each side.

The competition with Saka, therefore, does not need to be understood as an attempt to take the starter's place. Arsenal need more than one player capable of deciding matches, especially in a long season, with the Premier League, the Champions League and domestic cups. The point is that Madueke is starting to offer arguments to be considered more than a simple replacement.

One detail of this transformation happened away from Arsenal. After being left out of an England squad, Madueke decided to use the international break to train individually. Instead of treating the period as a chance to rest, the forward sought out a specific preparation programme.

Arteta highlighted the player's reaction as an example for the rest of the squad. The manager noted that Madueke came back from the break as a different athlete, determined not to accept the situation he was in.

Madueke at Arsenal, season by season.

According to recent reports, premier League 2025-26 vs. 2026-27, per-90 averages.

Premier League games only. Because the seasons have different numbers of minutes, the comparison uses per-90 averages; the total appears below each average. The change compares the averages. Madueke has not yet provided an assist in the Premier League in 2026-27. Data up to 21 November 2026 (matchweek 11).

According to recent reports, 'He went away, decided to train, came back, and he was a different Noni. You could sense that he meant business, and he was not going to accept that situation. Since then, he has been incredible' - Arteta explained, commenting on the player's change of attitude.

Sources indicate that the individual work, however, did not start now. In an interview with Sky Sports, Madueke revealed that he has been working for years with specialist coach Saul Isaksson-Hurst, since his time at PSV. The partnership involves technical improvement and individual development, with special attention to the ability to be more decisive in the final third.

According to recent reports, the result has shown up in the numbers: his average of chances created has more than doubled compared with last season, reaching 3.57 per 90 minutes in the Premier League. His dribble success rate has risen from 50% to 55%, while his passing accuracy has gone from 78% to 87%. In open-play crosses, his success rate has jumped from 14% to 33%.

It has been revealed that these numbers help explain why Arteta talks about a more complete player. Madueke has not stopped looking for the dribble, but he has started to execute better other actions that previously could limit his influence. The progress has come from different reasons and paths, but the result has arrived and is evident in the current season.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Vincent Kompany quipped Bayern Munich are missing "130 goals from last season" ahead of their Champions League trip to Lille, with Harry Kane and Michael Olise unavailable.

Bayern arrive at Stade Pierre-Mauroy just days after it was confirmed that Ballon d'Or winner Kane is set to miss the next few months with an ankle ligament injury sustained against Koln.

Kane has either scored or assisted in each of his last 11 games in the Champions League, which is right now the joint-longest run, along with Cristiano Ronaldo (between 2017 and 2018) and Ruud van Nistelrooy (between 2002 and 2003).

The England captain has 10 goals and 11 assists in all competitions this season, with Kompany also without Olise, who has failed to recover from an concern with his foot.

Olise has 18 goal involvements (12 goals, six assists) across all competitions this season, the sixth-highest tally across Europe's top five leagues in 2026-27.

It has been revealed that kane and Olise join an extensive list of injuries for Kompany to contend with. Serge Gnabry, Ismael Saibari, Alphonso Davies and Manuel Neuer are also sidelined.

Bayern have scored in each of their last 25 Champions League matches, dating back to January 2025, but he said they must find different ways to attack against Lille.

"It's about always being realistic and finding solutions – then getting the results," Kompany told reporters.

It has been revealed that "130 goals from last season aren't there, but we have guys who can run and fight. Then we have our fans too. We're going into the match with hunger and desire.

"We want to show that we're Bayern Munich on the pitch.".

Next up: back under the Champions League lights. https://t.co/xYqATNhcpq.

— FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) November 22, 2026.

Kompany did, however, have some good news on the injury front, with Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz both expected to play at least some part in Wednesday's clash.

The only previous meetings between Lille and Bayern came in the group stage of the 2012-13 Champions League, with the Germans winning home (6-1) and away (1-0).

Since the start of last season, Bayern's only two defeats in 18 Champions League matches (W13 D3) have been against the 2026 finalists Paris Saint-Germain (April this year) and Arsenal (November 2025).

And they come up against a Lille side who are on a six-game winless run in Europe (D1 L5). Only once have they had a longer run without a victory in major European competition (13 games between December 2012 and December 2019).

"Until last week, they were second in France. They always have a lot of talent; they're well known for their academy," Kompany said of Lille.

"They have a lot of pace on the counter; they defend aggressively from the front. They've got a few guys with international experience as well.

"They'll want to put on a show at home. I expect high pressure and a good game for the spectators.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 13:28 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 14:28 EST, 23 November 2026.

Celtic have accepted a reduced ticket allocation for their upcoming visit to Tynecastle despite calls from fans to reject the offer.

The Parkhead club, however, have stated that they will contact the Scottish Professional Football League over the issue.

Celtic will receive 508 tickets for the Premiership encounter on November 29, which will be their first visit to Tynecastle since beating Hearts to the title in the final stages of last season, a victory which resulted in a pitch invasion from some of their fans at Celtic Park.

A Celtic statement read: 'As supporters will know, our allocation for our forthcoming match against Heart of Midlothian at Tynecastle Stadium has been cut by 20 per cent, compared to our previous visit.

Industry observers note that 'There have been a variety of views expressed to the club from supporters in relation to accepting this allocation. Some groups representing travelling supporters explained to the club that their members did not wish to accept the tickets because of the reduced allocation.

'We have taken that into consideration and also raised their concerns with the home club, who have assured us that they have spoken to Police Scotland.

Hearts had stated that only 508 tickets will be made available for Celtic fans on November 29.

'Having carefully considered all of the circumstances, we can confirm we will accept the allocation of 508 tickets.

'We respect all views and opinions on this matter, and while we are concerned and disappointed at this reduction, and others across recent years, we feel it is vital that the team has the backing of our fans within the stadium for an important match.

'We realise the difficulties such a reduction can cause and in light of our discussions with supporters, we can confirm that should any supporter who is successful in the ballot, but does not wish to accept this ticket, then this will NOT affect the away ticket record moving forward.

'We thank our fans for their continued support and can confirm that we will be discussing the matter further with both the home club and the SPFL.'.

Celtic and Rangers formerly received the full Roseburn Stand for their supporters at Tynecastle, which resulted in an allocation of almost 3,500 tickets.

However, that figure was reduced to about 1,250 tickets in the 2021-22 season amid increased demand from home fans after the lockdown, and was further cut by about half.

Only Hibernian now get the full Roseburn Stand in a reciprocal agreement between the Edinburgh rivals.

Tynecastle has a capacity of about 20,000 but Hearts’ attendances are normally around 18,700 as a number of seats are not in use to create a barrier between the home and away fans.

Visiting clubs get about 800 tickets for games at Celtic Park, which has a 60,000 capacity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 08:40, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 08:42.

James Tarkowski received his first-ever red card in the Premier League as Everton fell to a heavy 4-0 defeat at Brentford on Monday night.

The 34-year-old defender had previously been given 74 yellow cards across 350 Premier League appearances but had never been sent off – a top-flight record for the most yellows without ever seeing red.

However, Tarkowski was dismissed in the first half with the Toffees trailing by two goals at the Gtech Community Stadium for a studs-up challenge on the shin of Yehor Yarmolyuk.

Tarkowski had initially thundered into a sliding challenge and won the ball, but his right boot followed through with his studs scraping down the Brentford midfielder’s leg.

On-field referee Craig Pawson gave a yellow card for the challenge, but was then advised by VAR to review the incident at the pitchside monitor, where he ultimately came to the decision to upgrade the yellow to a red.

Tarkowski was deemed to have “committed a challenge that endangers his opponent's safety” with a red card issued for serious foul play.

James Tarkowski is sent off! ? https://t.co/s5ta4f74np.

Tarkowski will therefore serve a three-match suspension and will crucially miss Sunday’s Merseyside derby against rivals Liverpool at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

The Toffees captain is also banned for a trip to Aston Villa on December 2 and a home clash with Fulham four days later, but he is available to return for an away fixture against Brighton & Hove Albion on December 13.

After taking charge of his record-breaking 593rd game as Everton manager, David Moyes was asked whether the club will look to appeal the red card, and he told Sky Sports: "Don't know yet.

"I thought Tarki got the ball in plenty of time, certainly got there before the player who came in late, but I think Tarki's foot was high, and in that case then there is a chance it can be given.".

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Moyes added: "My thoughts at the time, I didn't think it was, but when I've looked at it again I think his foot high. Is there enough force for it to be a red card? Not sure about that.".

Sky Sports pundit and former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher believes that Tarkowski was right to be sent off and feels that Moyes has a “substantial problem” to deal with ahead of the Merseyside derby.

According to recent reports, "It is a red card. It might not have been a red card in 1996, but it is in 2026,” Carragher remarked on Monday Night Football.

According to recent reports, "He knows what he's doing, and he doesn't need to do that. At the last moment, he is trying to pull back on the intensity of the challenge. Don't give [the referee] the option. He doesn't need to do that. I've made tackles like that.".

He added: "David Moyes should be looking at him and thinking [it's 2-0], you've left your mates out there with 10, and it's the Merseyside derby next.

Recent findings suggest that "For me, it's the biggest game of the season. Everton, biggest game of the season. I hope for the Liverpool players and staff, the biggest game of the season.

In a recent development, "He's brilliant in the box, and that will be a substantial problem for Everton. He's so good set-piece-wise.".

Either Jake O'Brien or Michael Keane is expected to play at centre-back alongside Jarrad Branthwaite in the absence of Tarkowski in the next three Premier League games.

A four-goal defeat for Everton has seen them slip to ninth in the Premier League table, with Brentford leapfrogging them into seventh position, albeit sitting just one point above them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

Sources indicate that “I don’t know,” Sage noted when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

It has been revealed that “We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old remarked. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”.

The Frenchman remarked that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

“I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he said. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

Industry observers note that “Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”.

Sage admitted that he will be assessing how Palace need to rethink their approach in the coming fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s trip to Besiktas in the Europa League.

“The first work to do is on me,” he remarked. “I’m responsible for what’s happened on the pitch, and I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing.

“It’s maybe in the preparation, in the way we give them the motivation to start the game just before in the locker room in the warm-up. We have to analyse that because it’s not normal. And today it was really at the highest level we cannot expect, and that’s the moment to change the thing.”.

Industry observers note that for all the scrutiny on his back three, Sage urged his entire side to take greater defensive responsibility, highlighting how the team were too passive in pressing Brighton. Palace have struggled to regain the solidity that long characterised the side since the departures of Marc Guéhi in January and Maxence Lacroix this summer.

Recent findings suggest that “The way of defending is not only on the back three; it is for every player, and there are some things to do collectively, too,” Sage said. “When we defend low we struggle a lot.”.

Industry observers note that sage joined Palace after a fine campaign with Lens. He led the club to second place in Ligue 1, just six points off Paris St-Germain, and victory in the Coupe de France. Yet, despite Sage’s reputation when he moved to Selhurst Park, his suitability for the Palace job is increasingly being questioned.

In a recent development, three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Sage could suffer the same fate, with doubts growing that he will still be in charge for Thursday’s trip to Besiktas.

It has been revealed that “It’s not my decision,” Sage remarked. “I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we are able to do better. And today the work is really important to do, and I will do it. It’s my job, and I’d like to change this.”.

It has been revealed that with only Manchester City and Arsenal above them, Brighton and Hove Albion are entitled to dream of making history. Yet, whatever happens between now and May, one accolade is already surely their own: the goal of the season award.

Industry observers note that diego Gómez’s 56-yard strike will instantly become the stuff of Brighton lore. The Paraguayan’s audacity will be even more cherished for coming against Crystal Palace, who were pummelled 5-0 in the M23 derby.

Recent findings suggest that all Premier League defeats are equal but some are more equal than others. Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Pierre Sage is at grave risk of suffering the same fate. But the hint of self-immolation in Palace’s display should not obscure the swagger of Brighton’s performance. Despite losing Danny Welbeck, last year’s top scorer, Brighton have scored 23 goals already this Premier League campaign, the most in the league. This tally includes one of the most extraordinary goals in Premier League history.

Most simply, Gómez’s goal, which put Brighton 2-0 up in the seventh minute, was a triumph of the imagination. Receiving a short pass from Olivier Boscagli just inside his own half, Gómez could have sought to pick out a team-mate. Instead, his scanning of the pitch before receiving the ball had revealed that goalkeeper Walter Benítez was off his line and Brighton’s attacking players were being tightly guarded by defenders. And so, just as he entered the centre circle in the opposition half, Gómez attempted the absurd.

“I’m not training with Diego Gómez shooting from 50 metres in training,” head coach Fabian Hürzeler said while breaking into a smile. “It’s just about making the players quick in their minds.

It has been revealed that “In these moments it’s about being very precise with his long kick. The perception to recognise the keeper and being quick to go to the action was impressive.”.

In a recent development, the presence of mind to attempt something outlandish was one thing; the execution was quite another. With Benítez vulnerable, Gómez took just one touch with his right foot before taking his shot, not giving the keeper enough time to scramble back to cover his line. As he looked up to confirm the opportunity, the 23-year-old struck the ball over Benítez with such venom that it did not even bounce until it reached the goal.

All that remained was for the Paraguayan international to hurtle towards the corner flag, engulfed by his ecstatic team-mates. For the Brighton fans, soaked by showers at the Amex, rain can never have felt so sweet.

Gómez’s goal will earn comparisons with David Beckham’s lob from the halfway line at Wimbledon. The advancements in pressing and conditioning in the 30 years since, with space ever more congested, makes such a strike even harder today. Not since Wayne Rooney in 2017 has a player scored a Premier League goal from further out than Gómez’s 56 yards.

According to recent reports, good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

Brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Brighton are third in the Premier League and were the division’s heaviest scorers after the last round of matches.

Industry observers note that yet the Palace nut has been a tough one to crack for Hürzeler, having not yet registered a win in four attempts. When asked what he enjoyed most about the rivalry, the German noted: “Nothing yet, because I didn’t win any games so far. Hopefully on Sunday this changes… I like these games because they’re derbies, more emotions, it’s a rivalry, it’s [us] against Crystal Palace.”.

According to recent reports, in his pre-match interview Hürzeler admitted to being an admirer of Pierre Sage, and while the Frenchman’s side have failed to match Brighton’s fast start, they rallied impressively to defeat rivals Nottingham Forest last weekend and fought back valiantly away at Lyon, albeit in a losing effort, in midweek. The return of Ismaïla Sarr from injury is a significant boost.

Industry observers note that elsewhere Bournemouth host Sunderland hoping to secure their first Premier League victory of the season. Marco Rose’s side and Tottenham are the only teams still without a win, but Bournemouth have been perfect in the Europa League and will look to transfer some of that momentum into the league. Sunderland scored late to win away at Portuguese side Torreense.

His profile has reportedly caught the attention of the Parisian hierarchy, especially as the player now shares the same agent as Achraf Hakimi.

Sources indicate that this could ease discussions. The rumour is also being followed closely in Barcelona, as a potential transfer of the Real Betis winger would allow Barcelona to recoup a significant sum.

The Catalan outlet recalls that in September 2023, Barcelona sold Abde to Real Betis for £6.4m (€7.5m). In that deal, they kept a share of the Moroccan's economic rights. Initially set at 50%, it was later reduced to 20% in February 2025 as part of the agreement concerning Vitor Roque.

It has been revealed that A £51m (€60m) transfer, the amount of Abde's release clause, would therefore bring Barcelona £10m. PSG would have the opportunity to sign a promising 24-year-old winger for a reasonable amount, while doing their Spanish rivals a serious financial favour by triggering the clause.

This sum could give the Barcelona hierarchy more room for manoeuvre to strengthen Hansi Flick's squad this winter. The German boss is notably looking to sign a centre-back.

But just as they did in the Premier League at Newcastle on Saturday, Arsenal were unable to see out the victory, with Maximilian Beier netting for the visitors after half-time.

Jobe Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside, while Gyokeres could perhaps count himself fortunate not to give away a penalty when a Dortmund corner struck him on the arm.

Gyokeres then wasted a golden opportunity to restore Arsenal’s advantage when he headed wide unmarked from six yards, while the ball cannoned off Serhou Guirassy to twice strike the Dortmund post in the closing stages. Declan Rice hit the woodwork again for Arsenal with five minutes left.

The draw leaves Arsenal fifth in the table, but they could be on the bubble of the top-eight places – which are assured of automatic qualification for the next phase – if results work against them on Wednesday.

Gyokeres was introduced only as a stoppage-time substitute in Arsenal’s 2-2 draw at St James’ Park despite the Gunners chasing the game for most of the second half.

Here, he began from the start and opened the scoring with his first meaningful contribution of the game.

Noni Madueke had time and space to bring down a crossfield ball before finding Gyokeres, who immediately tried his luck from range, and perhaps catching Gregor Kobel in the visiting goal by surprise.

But that was to take away nothing from the velocity and dip behind Gyokeres’ effort – the sort of strike which encouraged Arsenal to spend £68million last summer but has not always been repaid. It was Gyokeres’ first at the Emirates since May.

Rice fired over from range and then only a last-ditch tackle from Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck denied the England midfielder moments later. Arsenal led at the break, but they did in the North East before a second-half collapse saw them emerge with just a point, rather than three.

He looked up to find Beier, who took one touch past Gabriel before unleashing a low drive. Kepa Arrizabalaga, deputising for the injured David Raya, never got close to saving it.

Piero Hincapie’s header was saved by Kobel as Arsenal mustered a response. Bellingham thought he had put Dortmund ahead when he turned away Kepa’s bungled save but the assistant referee’s offside flag came to Arsenal’s rescue.

In all, the Gunners had 29 shots but only four of those were on target, and the need for a world-class finisher remains a top priority should Arsenal want to win the Champions League for the first time in their history. They will face Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid next.

Ex-England striker Carlton Cole has slammed Manchester United’s recruitment under INEOS and claims it was ‘criminal’ the club didn’t explore a move for Danny Welbeck in the summer.

There had been a sense of optimism amongst United’s fanbase heading into the season after Michael Carrick picked up the pieces from Ruben Amorim’s turbulent reign to lead the club to a third-place finish last term.

But the Red Devils once again find themselves in a state of disarray after a wretched start to the 2026/27 campaign, which ultimately cost Carrick his job earlier this month.

With genuine fears growing that United could become embroiled in a relegation scrap, Mauricio Pochettino has been tasked with steadying the ship and steering a dispirited squad away from the bottom of the Premier League table.

The Argentine’s tenure got off to a nightmare start at the weekend, though, as his side were put to the sword at the hands of arch-rivals Liverpool in a thumping 4-0 defeat at Anfield.

Sunday’s result ensured United remain firmly in the drop zone after 11 matches, only one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace with the worst defensive record of any team in Europe’s top five leagues.

If Pochettino was expecting to be supported with significant financial backing in his efforts to turn United’s fortunes around this winter, he will likely be disappointed.

After all, Reports this week suggest the 54-year-old will have a budget of ‘well under £50million’ to work with when the January transfer window opens for business.

Sources indicate that asked what Pochettino must address with his meagre funds while tackling United’s woes on The Dressing Room Podcast, Cole replied: ‘The spine. They haven’t got a striker, a worthy striker.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Midfield, I think they’re alright there for now because they’ve got Carlos Baleba and I think he’s a fantastic player by the way, they’ve got Kobbie Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes… I think they’re alright in that position.

According to recent reports, ‘I know the boy from Chelsea, Andrey Santos, he’s there, but I know he’s not tuned in yet because it’s high pressure right now and he’s a little bit off it. They’ve got Youri Tielemans as well. Then you’ve got the centre-backs…’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to Cole, United missed a trick when they gave Chelsea a free run at signing Welbeck from Brighton in the summer.

‘I think it’s criminal they didn’t sign Welbeck,’ he added.

It has been revealed that ‘I think he’s wasted at Chelsea at the moment, they should have signed Welbeck. He’d have done alright!’.

Eyebrows were raised when Pochettino named his team to face Liverpool on Sunday, with Matthijs de Ligt thrown in for his first Premier League start of the campaign.

There were signs of rustiness in De Ligt’s game from minute one and it was the Dutchman’s calamitous defending that led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s breakthrough – and Leny Yoro’s sending off – after only ten minutes.

‘I thought that was him [Pochettino] protesting already,’ Cole said of De Ligt’s surprise selection.

‘I think it was on the first or second day that he was in, he was already saying he wanted more control in the transfer market. I thought you negotiated that in your deal!

‘He’s chosen the right time to do it [make a protest], in a game like that.

‘This was a free hit for him and yes, he needs defenders. But I’ve noted it before, INEOS have gone with signing forward first and then the next window they get a midfielder… who does that? So that’s what has happened.’.

Cole went a step further on Pochettino’s decision to field De Ligt, adding: ‘I think it’s bang out of order, he’s been stitched up.

‘He’s obviously not fit, he can’t read it. When you’ve been out so long, you get your bearings wrong, you don’t know where you are on the pitch. It happens, right? So I give him grace for that.

‘The problem is that Yoro is not experienced. So if you’re going to bring in De Ligt, you’ve got to bring another experienced defender in with him.

‘If De Ligt is going to be there and Harry Maguire is there then it’s alright and if Maguire makes that mistake that Yoro made, I get it.

Recent findings suggest that ‘But Yoro is still young, he’s still learning the game. They’re both, to some extent, inexperienced at this moment in time so it’s the blind leading the blind.’.

United will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters away to Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Three days later, Pochettino’s men return to Premier League action at home to Brentford.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes insists the incentive of next month's Premier Sports Cup Final can fuel his players as they prepare to embark on a vital run of fixtures.

A 2-1 triumph over Motherwell on Saturday night stretched Rangers' unbeaten run to 13 matches after Ryan Naderi struck a late winner at Fir Park.

McInnes' side will host a revitalised Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday night, before two further home matches against Falkirk and Dundee United over the next week.

They will then face a double-header against Hibs, with a league clash at Easter Road swiftly followed by the cup final.

McInnes insists no player is guaranteed their place in the team - and challenged them to earn their place for the Hampden showpiece as they look to win the first trophy of the season.

'I think the squad looks strong at the minute,' noted the Ibrox boss. 'We've got good options and good options from the bench to turn to.

Derek McInnes has led Rangers on a 13-game unbeaten run in all competitions.

'In this little run of fixtures, hopefully everybody will start to play a wee bit more of their part and hopefully more winning performances.

'I don't think I'll mention it [the cup final] too often, but they are not daft, they see that and everybody wants to play in the team.

'Anybody who's in the team needs to keep playing well to stay in the team and anybody who's not in the team needs to train right and take advantage of their minutes.

It has been revealed that 'We make that point often enough. Sometimes you've got to go away to tough venues like Motherwell and do the hard work and get the reward.

'But there's bigger games, more games like cup finals to take part in, so everybody wants to play in that one.

According to recent reports, 'I'm sure it does us no harm. I think it keeps the fans bubbling along, a chance of silverware, so when it comes along hopefully, as I say, we're in good form.'.

Rangers are on a strong run of form and haven't lost a game since they were dumped out of Europe against Jablonec at the end of August.

The victory over Motherwell maintained their position in second in the table, four points adrift of Celtic with a game in hand.

Up against an Aberdeen side buoyed by their first win under new boss Mario Frick at the weekend, McInnes wants his players to keep the pedal to the metal.

'I think it's unusual with five games now away from Ibrox, four in the league and the cup game, and now the fixtures kind of run the other way,' said the Rangers boss.

'We've got some good fixtures at home but I think we always look at little blocks in the weeks, and where we're looking to try and get to by a certain period, and get certain points and certain targets.

'But first thing's first now with Aberdeen. We've got to make sure we're a strong home team again. Hopefully we can score a few more goals but, ultimately, as long as we win the game, I'll be happy.

'I think there's always a wee concern when you've got so many away on an international break, but obviously now with the January break gone, this is us working right through to March.

'When you look at those little blocks of games, and where the teams are, it's key that we just put our shoulder to the wheel.

Recent findings suggest that 'Every game is going to bring up different challenges and just because we're at Ibrox, it's an advantage, but it doesn't guarantee anything. We've got to use that advantage properly.

'As I say, we've got some fixtures now ahead of the cup final. Hopefully we can get into the cup final in good form and with some strong performances.'.

Venezuelan striker Kevin Kelsy could be in line to start against Aberdeen.

Kevin Kelsy could be in line for a bigger role this week after fatigue caused by his return from international duty limited his involvement in Saturday's win over Motherwell.

The Venezuela striker was only fit enough for a substitute appearance after enduring a gruelling journey back from a friendly in Russia, with Derek McInnes admitting the travel disruption had taken its toll.

'When you go away on international duty, they go to some far-flung places and playing a friendly in Russia is not the best preparation,' said the Rangers boss.

Recent findings suggest that 'There was a point on Thursday morning when we were really worried about whether he was getting back. To have ten-and-a-half hours in an airport all day Thursday isn't ideal preparation.

According to recent reports, 'He was gubbed on Friday. He was very tired when he spoke to me and told me he hadn't really slept.

'It's been a bit unusual, the preparation. We sent him home early on Friday to get a good sleep and look after himself, but we just made the call we thought was the right thing to do.

'We needed everybody at it on Saturday and we've got a substantial week ahead of us where he can play his part, hopefully from the start in one or two of these games.'.

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 09:01, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 10:51.

Kevin De Bruyne has made his feelings for Manchester City crystal clear as he has spoken out for the first time since the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations.

At the end of September, an independent commission found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the investigation.

The Citizens are accused of using "sham" contracts with a number of commercial partners to disguise secret funding of more than £830m and artificially inflate revenues between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

Man City continue to plead their innocence and lodged an appeal last month, stating that “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.”.

A plethora of possible sanctions have been mooted should Man City’s guilty verdict be upheld, including heavy fines, transfer bans, stripping titles, points deductions leading to relegation and expulsion from the Premier League.

De Bruyne spent 10 glorious years at the Etihad Stadium before leaving in the summer of 2025 and will go down as one of Man City’s greatest-ever players after playing a crucial role in the club winning 19 trophies during his time at the club.

The Belgian playmaker won six Premier League titles, five EFL Cups and three FA Cups, while he also won the Champions League during a historic treble-winning season in 2022-23.

The two-time Premier League Player of the Season scored 108 goals and provided 177 assists in 422 appearances for Man City across all competitions, with 119 of those assists recorded in the Premier League to rank him second on the all-time list behind Ryan Giggs (162).

De Bruyne has made a welcome retuned to Manchester as his current club Napoli prepare to face City in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

While De Bruyne has acknowledged that some people may have different opinions over Man City’s guilty verdict, the legendary midfielder himself has insisted that his feelings towards the club will “never change”.

Recent findings suggest that "My feeling's never been different,” he told reporters at a press conference. “Honestly, the way that I feel is just the way that I've been treated by this club, what I've done with this club for me personally, and how we've worked together as a group. Of course, it's a lot of things that's been going on but I cannot change anything about that.

"I'm proud of what I've done as a football player, and honestly... This is my club! I love the owners, I've talked about a lot of stuff outside of football, I've even spoken to Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] how to buy a club and everything, so there's a lot of things that goes around after this.

"I've nothing but affection for this club and that will never change! Even now, the people who treated me for 10 years exceptionally, my family and everything, that's for me the most important and for me, that is it to be honest.".

Intense criticism has been aimed at Man City since the guilty verdict, but De Bruyne cannot "change anything" about people calling his former club a "disgrace" and still believes that everything he personally achieved with the club was won fairly.

Sources indicate that “It [the verdict] still doesn’t change, my football has not changed,” De Bruyne noted. “In life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit.

Industry observers note that “I played in between the white lines, I competed with other players and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players. That’s the thing I value most.

“In my career, the most notable thing is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things.

Industry observers note that “I’ve given my all and that’s not going to change in my mind. I don’t think a lot of ­people will change in their mind how they view me as a player or how we played. Other people may be disgraced a bit, but I can’t change anything about that.”.

Tuesday’s contest will mark De Bruyne’s second appearance back at the Etihad since departing Man City, and the 35-year-old will be hoping for a much smoother evening this time around.

On his previous visit last year, a first-half red card forced ex-Napoli boss Antonio Conte to reshuffle his side, with De Bruyne the unfortunate player to be sacrificed early in a 2-0 defeat.

What do various cancers have in common?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, cancers arising in distinct organs differ in their cellular organization, genetic alterations and patterns of how they progress1. Now, a large-scale analysis reveals striking similarities between the non-malignant cells found in the tumour microenvironment (TME) — the local environment in and around a tumour, in which non-malignant cells interact with cancer cells — across various types of cancer. Writing in Nature, Januszyk et al.2 integrate single-cell data from 42 types of tumour in humans and mice. The authors identify recurring patterns of gene activity in immune cells and in stromal cells, which contribute to tissue structure and function. These similarities provide a starting point for testing whether treatments directed at the non-cancerous cells of the TME might be effective across a range of cancer types.

Monza star Gustavo Varela has distanced himself from speculation that he could be set for a January transfer move and insists he is ‘paying no attention’ to incessant rumours linking him with Arsenal, Barcelona and Napoli.

Varela, 21, was deemed surplus to requirements at Benfica and completed a switch to newly promoted Italian outfit Monza for a fee of just €2million (£1.7m) – plus performance-related bonuses – in the summer.

It has proven a tough start to the season for Monza on their return to Serie A, with the club picking up just three wins and languishing down in 14th place in the table.

Varela has proven a shining light up front, though, scoring 11 goals in his opening 11 top-flight appearances, and the striker’s barnstorming form in Lombardy has begun to attract the attentions of European football’s elite.

According to recent reports emanating out of Varela’s native Portugal, Barca, Napoli and Arsenal are all actively pursuing a deal for the forward on the back of his goalscoring exploits in the first three months of the campaign.

Premier League champions Arsenal are noted to be among a host of Premier League clubs that have ‘expressed an interest’ in Varela and were ‘one of the first to enquire’ about the player’s potential availability.

It’s understood the Gunners are in the market for an attacker of Varela’s profile, with Viktor Gyokeres struggling to live up to expectations following his £64m arrival from Sporting last year.

On Monday night, Varela ensured he remained in the headlines with a terrific brace in Monza’s 3-0 victory over Fiorentina – in doing so, becoming only the third player in the last 50 years to reach the double figures in their first 11 Serie A games.

Industry observers note that ‘I can’t believe what I’m doing. I go home, close my eyes and I can’t believe it. Football is made of moments,’ Varela told DAZN Italy following Monza’s win.

In a recent development, ‘A very beautiful cross came in, I was close to the goal and I decided to try my luck. If you don’t try, you can’t do it, and it happened.’.

Varela was then asked for his reaction the rumoured interest he was receiving from some of Europe’s most high-profile teams, to which he responded: ‘I continue to thank Monza for allowing me to be here. It has all been incredible.

‘I feel lucky to be part of this reality and I only hope to continue on this path.

‘I pay no attention to the news. I only focus on what I have to do on the field. It’s normal, it’s part of football.

‘I’m going through a great moment but a less good moment may arise tomorrow.

Trust us, you're going to want to watch this OUTRAGEOUS finish from Gustavo Varela 😮‍💨🔥#MonzaFiorentina #UNROSSOALLAVIOLENZA pic.twitter.com/Z2RvJFul6X.

‘That’s why I try to simply enjoy the present without paying attention to the news.

Monza are believed to have slapped an asking price on Varela in the region of €40-50m (£33-42m).

Though they did not insert a buy-back clause in their deal with Monza for Varela, Benfica will be entitled to 20 per cent of any future transfer fee for the sought-after youngster.

The Primeira Liga club also have the right of first refusal should a bidding war break out for the Portugal Under-21 international, who was named the Serie A Rising Star of the Month for October.

Varela’s current contract with Monza runs through to June 2030.

  • Arsenal will be bidding to equal two all-time Champions League records when they welcome Borussia Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium for Tuesday's league-phase encounter.
  • Mikel Arteta's men reunite with the German giants 12 years on from their last head-to-head in November 2014, when the Spaniard captained Arsenal to a 2-0 victory in North London.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 09:09.

Arsenal will be bidding to equal two all-time Champions League records when they welcome Borussia Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium for Tuesday's league-phase encounter.

Mikel Arteta's men reunite with the German giants 12 years on from their last head-to-head in November 2014, when the Spaniard captained Arsenal to a 2-0 victory in North London.

The Gunners could end the evening top of the Champions League league phase table too, if they overcome Dortmund and Real Madrid - who are two points clear - either lose to PSV Eindhoven or draw and fall behind on goal difference; Paris Saint-Germain are not in action until Wednesday.

Arsenal have accrued 10 points from their opening four continental games this season, overcoming Lille, Slavia Prague and Napoli and only dropping points in an encapsulating 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich.

After also navigating the entire 2025-26 league phase unbeaten, Arsenal could firstly equal their own club record of 17 straight Champions League group stage/league phase games without suffering defeat.

Arteta's men have won 15 and drawn one of their 16 league-phase games since a 1-0 loss to Inter Milan in November 2024, and they have only ever gone 17 unbeaten at this stage between 2003 and 2006.

That record streak began with a 1-0 victory over Dynamo Kyiv in November 2003, and ended when Arsene Wenger's men suffered a 1-0 defeat to CSKA Moscow in 2006.

Additionally, Arsenal have won each of their last 12 Champions League group stage/league phase games at the Emirates and could equal the English football record for the longest victorious run on home soil.

The only Premier League team to win more successive UCL league phase/group stage games at home is Liverpool, who triumphed in 13 on the spin between 2020 and 2025.

Ever since their return to the Champions League in the 2023-24 season, Arsenal have been almost perfect at home in the group stage/league phase, and their 12-game winning run is a sight to behold.

Arteta's side kicked off their triumphant streak with a 4-0 rout of PSV Eindhoven in September 2023, before Sevilla and Lens were bested in the same year.

The 2024-25 group stage saw Paris Saint-Germain, Shakhtar Donetsk, Monaco and Dinamo Zagreb conquered in North London, while Olympiacos, Bayern Munich, Atletico Madrid and Kairat Almaty fell to Arsenal's Emirates might in 2025-26.

The Gunners' only home encounter in Europe so far this season ended in a 3-0 success over Lille, and they have scored a remarkable 36 goals while conceding just three during their 12-match sequence.

Thanks to Arsenal's prolonged absence from the Champions League between 2017 and 2023, it has been almost exactly 10 years since they last failed to win a group stage/league phase game at the Emirates; a 2-2 draw with Paris Saint-Germain on November 23, 2016.

With thinner stripes than the current home shirt – modelled on the 1998-99 Scudetto shirt – it’ll also feature a collar for the first time since the 2018-19 season.

With this set to be the last home shirt before the return to Adidas, it certainly does Puma a lot of credit and it will hopefully round off the 10-year stint in style.

Michael Carrick’s successor is noted to be keen on adding a striker to his ranks to cover for the injured Benjamin Sesko, but tightening up his backline will also represent a priority.

Fulham’s Calvin Bassey emerged as a potential target last week, but the versatile defender is reported to be close to signing a contract extension with the London club.

While reinforcements would certainly aid United’s cause, former club captains Roy Keane and Gary Neville fear it is not just defenders their old side are in need of.

Nicky Butt believes that Liverpool will prove to be Arsenal’s main title challengers over the likes of Manchester City this season.

Defending champions Arsenal extended their lead at the top of the table to six points after a hard-fought draw away at Newcastle.

Manchester City did snap their three-match losing streak, but a 1-1 draw on Fulham means Enzo Maresca’s side are now winless in four Premier League matches and also six points off the league leaders.

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 09:31.

Struggling on the pitch, Manchester United are already preparing for the January transfer window with three positions targeted and seven options identified.

19th in the Premier League, Manchester United are going through a sporting crisis. Mauricio Pochettino has just arrived to replace Michael Carrick. The Argentinian boss will try to halt the negative spiral, while the hierarchy is already preparing its next January transfer window.

The Manchester club intend to use January to strengthen their squad. According to TeamTalk, the club's decision-makers have identified three priority positions: centre-back, left-back and centre-forward. Signing a centre-back is Manchester United's main priority.

The club already have three profiles in mind: Calvin Bassey (Fulham), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton) and Nathan Collins (Brentford).

The club's executives have reportedly already made enquiries about all three players. A permanent transfer would, however, be needed to convince any of these clubs, with a loan not being considered in these cases.

A large part of the winter budget should therefore be devoted to this signing. Manchester United's January budget is reportedly £50m, according to the Daily Mail. That is a rather small amount to strengthen in three positions and cover for the shortcomings of a squad in the midst of doubt.

Recent findings suggest that in attack, Manchester United want to sign a centre-forward capable of providing more competition. Two options stand out: Folarin Balogun (Monaco) and Ivan Toney (Al-Ahli). A loan with an option to buy is reportedly being considered for both forwards, while Joshua Zirkzee could leave in January.

The club want to provide an additional solution on the left flank, where Luke Shaw lacks competition and availability.

Two players are particularly liked: Alejandro Balde (Barcelona) and Rayan Ait-Nouri (Manchester City). Talks have reportedly already taken place with both clubs.

Both full-backs could leave in January as they play little at their respective clubs. Manchester United would favour a loan for one of these deals. The club have therefore already drawn up their roadmap, but the sporting situation and the meagre budget will not make it easy for them to strengthen.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Arsenal dropped two points in their 1-1 Champions League draw against Borussia Dortmund, so claims Noni Madueke.
  • The Gunners were dominant in the first half at Emirates Stadium, where Viktor Gyokeres' stunner put them into a 10th-minute lead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Arsenal dropped two points in their 1-1 Champions League draw against Borussia Dortmund, so claims Noni Madueke.

The Gunners were dominant in the first half at Emirates Stadium, where Viktor Gyokeres' stunner put them into a 10th-minute lead.

Yet Arsenal could not add to their lead, and Dortmund stepped up in the second half, equalising in the 55th minute through Maximilian Beier.

Jobe Bellingham saw a goal disallowed, but Arsenal came on strong late on, with Gyokeres squandering a golden chance, while the Gunners hit the post twice.

Arsenal's 30 shots are their most on record in a Champions League game (since 2003-04), and the Gunners' most in a game that they failed to win across all competitions since December 2023 v West Ham.

And while Madueke felt some of Arsenal's play was "incredible", he acknowledged Mikel Arteta's team are frustrated.

He told Amazon Prime: "I feel like the performance from us up until the last shot was incredible at times.

"Definitely feels like two points dropped. A bit of frustration; need to get all three points, I think.".

Honours even in N5. https://t.co/quJELEQP8x.

— Arsenal (@Arsenal) November 24, 2026.

Gyokeres echoed Madueke's sentiment, though he is confident Arsenal will get better results if they keep on creating so many chances.

"We could have scored in the second half. We could have won the game in many different ways," he told Amazon Prime.

"We played well and created a lot of chances, we deserved to win the game but sometimes it is like that.

"The most crucial thing is that we create those chances and get shots on goal. For sure we will score goals.".

Arsenal have failed to win a home game in the group stage of major European competition for the first time since November 2019 (2-1 defeat v Eintracht Frankfurt), ending a run of 18 successive victories – the longest such winning run by any side in major European competition history.

Arteta mentioned: "The performance was superb and there is no question about that from the start to the end. We played against a really good side and the domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more.

"I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.".

The Gunners are, though, only the third English side in Champions League history to go 20 successive matches unbeaten (W14 D6), after Manchester City between 2022 and 2024 (26) and Manchester United between 2007 and 2009 (25).

Now, their focus will turn to a huge Premier League clash with Man City on Sunday.

"I think these are the best games. I'm really looking forward to it," Madueke added.

"Two draws on the bounce now and I just desperately want to win on the weekend and I know my team-mates feel the same.

Sources indicate that "We are going to do everything we have to win the three points. We're champions, we're at home. We have a duty to perform well at the Emirates. There are things we need to improve but all in all we are going in the right direction.".

Scotland's World Cup prize must not become a missed opportunity

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (584 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Confirmation that Scotland will co-host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is an undoubted boost for the game in this country.
  • Staging a global showpiece with England, Wales and Northern Ireland is indeed a potential game-changer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 23 November 2026.

Confirmation that Scotland will co-host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is an undoubted boost for the game in this country.

Staging a global showpiece with England, Wales and Northern Ireland is indeed a potential game-changer.

The joint bid projected that the competition would attract 3.5billion viewers worldwide. And that 4.5m tickets would be sold across the host nations.

But the key for Scotland will be the impact it has on girls taking up the sport, supporters watching it and professionals playing it north of the Border.

Scotland captain Caroline Weir has already described it as a ‘pivotal’ moment, a ‘real opportunity’ to drive momentum and reach another level, domestically and internationally.

Industry observers note that she’s right. It is an opportunity, of the once-in-a-lifetime variety, but a word of caution is in order. Opportunities are not enough in themselves to be transformative.

They have to be embraced, exploited and squeezed for all they are worth so that every last drop of their potential is properly fulfilled.

Star player Caroline Weir believes co-hosting the World Cup could be pivotal for women's football in Scotland.

It would be criminal if the powers-that-be got complacent about this priceless gift and made assumptions about its long-term legacy.

More players, more fans and more media coverage would be hugely exciting, but it will all be wasted if not supported by facilities, coaches and the safeguarding that goes with it.

In a recent development, it has happened before. Interest in athletics rocketed after Glasgow 2014, but a poor infrastructure, which continued to rely on volunteers, prevented a grassroots boom.

And how many times have we heard Judy Murray complain that Scottish tennis squandered the opportunity presented to it by her son, Andy?

In a recent development, scotland’s women played at the World Cup in 2019. Their game has grown since then, but the national side have not been to another major tournament and the domestic product is still a shadow of its English counterpart.

According to recent reports, only a handful of Scottish teams have full-time players. The wages are way behind those on offer down south. And professional men’s clubs could do much, much more to develop the sport. It’s no wonder the Scottish league can’t keep its better players.

The opposite is true in England, where the success of the national team is often attributed to the level of investment by the FA and the backing of sponsors across the country.

The good news is that Scotland have made a start on that front with something called Project 2035, which aims to transform girls' and women’s football over the next decade.

The Scottish government has stumped up an initial £250,000 to help with the 10-year blueprint, which outlined a number of key objectives earlier this month.

They want to grow participation at grassroots level, increase the number of women working in football - as coaches, leaders and decision-makers - and quadruple the number of fans. The hope also is that Scotland will progress beyond the group stage of at least one World Cup by 2035.

Sources indicate that having those ambitions is one thing; making good on them is quite another. The government, the league, clubs and the ruling body: all should be thrilled by this opportunity but they should also feel the pressure that it brings. For it is their responsibility, their duty, to make the most of it.
